teachingReview.heading: Validate the complete formulation
teachingReview.body: Calcium-phosphate solubility depends on amino-acid product and concentration, calcium and phosphate salts, pH, cysteine, other electrolytes, final volume, temperature, sequence, time, and storage. A clear bag does not prove safety. Use validated compatibility data and compounding-system limits for the exact formulation.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF pages1-2 compatibility/stability and product-specific amino-acid curves, volume, cysteine
PDF pages1-2 electrolyte/acidic interactions, validated mixing sequence and storage
PDF page4 section2.3 pH/temperature/relative ions, sequence and refrigeration; page5 section5.2 postfilter precipitation

teachingReview.heading: Do not force a total nutrient admixture
teachingReview.body: ASPEN notes that a total nutrient admixture is often not feasible for pediatric patients because high calcium and phosphorus requirements create compatibility and stability constraints. Lipid is commonly infused separately or co-administered by a validated Y-site process. Product-specific compatibility remains required.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF page2 Table1 emulsion instability/calcium-phosphate risk and separate ILE
PDF page1 Figure2 Y-site process; prior pediatric lipid tool whole-body closure retained

teachingReview.heading: Calculate the aluminum burden
teachingReview.body: Aluminum contamination can enter PN through large- and small-volume components. Immature kidneys and prolonged exposure increase neurologic and bone toxicity risk. The July 2025 FDA draft, written for product sponsors and applicants, proposes limiting total PN exposure to 4 to 5 mcg/kg/day. It remains a nonbinding draft, not a finalized implementation standard. The product-label warning states that tissue loading can occur below this range. Check each component's aluminum information and sum all sources; a labeled maximum gives an exposure estimate, not proof of the amount actually present.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF pages4-12 and16-19 draft/regulatory label and maximum-at-expiry context
PDF page6 section5.5 prolonged exposure, kidney immaturity, CNS/bone and lower-rate loading

teachingReview.heading: Protect the entire administration path
teachingReview.body: ASPEN recommends a 1.2 micron filter for total nutrient admixtures, dextrose-amino acid admixtures, and lipid emulsions. For premature infants, protect the PN bag and infusion set from compounding through infusion, including lipid-free PN. Verify the patient, route, pump channel and rate, line connection, filter, and light-protection setup before administration.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF pages1-2 1.2 micron scope
PDF page1 patient/line/pump/light-protection checks
Executive Summary and Methods definition complete container/set, lipid-free PN, beginning at compounding

teachingReview.heading: Keep the filter in the safety path
teachingReview.body: Place a 1.2 micron filter near the catheter hub, below the Y-site where separately infused lipid and dextrose-amino acid solutions join. A filter does not replace compatibility review or infection-control practices. If pressure alarms suggest occlusion, check the tubing, clamps, catheter, and filter size. Replace an occluded filter with one of the same pore size and ask the pharmacist to review the formulation. Never bypass the filter to keep PN running.

sourceEvidence.locator: PDF page1 Figure2 and page2 occlusion response, no unfiltered continuation
PDF page1 distal filter and asepsis

teachingReview.heading: Calculate aluminum from concentration and volume
teachingReview.body: For a stated example, a 2 kg infant receives 60 mL/day of a component labeled at 25 mcg/L and 3 mL/day of another labeled at 3,500 mcg/L. Divide each concentration by 1,000 to convert to mcg/mL. The contributions are 1.5 and 10.5 mcg/day: 12 mcg/day total, or 6 mcg/kg/day. These are example concentrations, not named-product doses. Count every other component before interpreting the total. Maximum label values estimate exposure; they do not establish actual aluminum content.
